target_moa.text: Elosulfase alfa is a recombinant human N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase, the lysosomal enzyme deficient in MPS IVA; it provides exogenous enzyme that hydrolyzes sulfate from keratan sulfate and chondroitin-6-sulfate, reducing their lysosomal accumulation

citations.quote: Elosulfase alfa is a recombinant human enzyme N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase that provides the action of cleaving sulfate esters from the glycosaminoglycans keratan sulfate and chondroitin 6-sulfate.
Without functional GALNS enzyme, the glycosaminoglycans keratan sulfate and chondroitin-6-sulfate are not degraded and accumulate within the cell lysosome.
Elosulfase alfa is a purified human enzyme produced by recombinant DNA technology in a Chinese hamster ovary cell line.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) are pyrexia (33% vs 14% placebo), vomiting (31% vs 7%), headache (26% vs 15%), nausea (24% vs 7%), abdominal pain (21% vs 2%), chills (10% vs 2%), and fatigue (10% vs 3%). Hypersensitivity reactions occurred in 44 of 235 (18.7%) patients, and 18 of 235 (7.7%) experienced signs/symptoms consistent with anaphylaxis

summary.text: Vimizim (elosulfase alfa), an enzyme replacement therapy for the rare lysosomal storage disease MPS IVA (Morquio A syndrome), received orphan product designation in May 2009 and was approved first-cycle under priority review on the basis of a single pivotal placebo-controlled trial (MOR-004) with the 6MWT primary endpoint, following review by the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC)

On November 19, 2013, the Division sought advice from the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) regarding the appropriateness of the 6MWT to assess treatment benefit in this patient population.
